items.title: Older Australians suffering under Labor’s ‘botched’ aged care at home program, inquiry finds
items.summary:
The Support at Home system has ‘baffling’ bureaucracy and ‘rations and denies care’, says Greens chair of Senate inquiry

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Many older Australians are dying before they can access home support, paying exorbitant fees, and being pushed into hospitals and residential care before they are ready because of a flawed federal government aged care program, a Senate inquiry has found.

The inquiry is examining the impact of the Support at Home program, which launched in November 2025 and has been plagued by complaints of making care harder to access and more expensive. The inquiry was due to finish in November, but has been extended for a further year after receiving almost 300 submissions.

New powers allowing defence officials to use lethal force against suspected trespassers into designated zones could have “significant” human rights implications, a Labor-chaired inquiry has warned.

The committee also raised concerns about a lack of requirements to ensure anyone detained under the new laws had access to fresh drinking water and humane conditions. Leah Blyth, federal Liberal senator for South Australia, has defected to One Nation, blindsiding former Coalition colleagues who called her a “turncoat” and raising further scrutiny of chaos inside the opposition.

items.title: Senior Liberal slams Blyth in email to members, saying ‘you gave her your trust, she threw it away’ – as it happened
items.summary:
• Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Pauline Hanson has released a statement this morning welcoming South Australian senator Leah Blyth to her party.

Blyth is the second high-profile federal defection from the Coalition to One Nation – after Barnaby Joyce.

Senator Blyth will be One Nation’s first South Australian Senator and will build on One Nation’s expanding support within the state.

My team and I are delighted to welcome Senator Blyth to sit in the Senate with One Nation.

We are facing at the next election clearly a coalition of the Liberals, Nationals and One Nation, with all the baggage that each of these parties brings to the table. They’re all anti-worker, they’re all extreme … this demonstrates, I think, more disunity in the Liberal party under Angus Taylor.

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents, a leading British lawyer has claimed, as Hong Kong prepares to host the police organisation’s general assembly for the first time.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”
